title: Power Apps: modernised Personal settings experience in model-driven apps
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, default state, licensing and documented settings match the sources checked. It correctly distinguishes Learn's already-default experience from the roadmap's development status, and its narrowly stated documentation gaps were confirmed by targeted searches.

claims.quote: The Personal settings experience in model-driven apps has been modernized with clearer organization, updated navigation, and a more consistent design.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The Appearance tab appears only when the app has the header and navigation refresh (wave 2) enabled.
claims.quote: Appearance settings require the header and navigation refresh (wave 2) to be enabled on the app. If the header and navigation refresh isn't turned on, the Appearance tab isn't shown and the app renders at the default appearance.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: The wave 2 qualifier is documented for the Appearance tab, not for the whole Personal settings redesign.
claims.quote: Searched: modern Personal settings header and navigation requirement; read set-personal-options and appearance-settings. The former calls modern settings the default; the latter attaches the requirement to Appearance settings. No whole-panel requirement found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Every user who runs a model-driven app needs a license providing Power Apps premium use rights.
claims.quote: Model-driven apps use Dataverse and are premium apps by default. Every user who runs a model-driven app needs a license that provides Power Apps premium use rights.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Power Apps Premium generally satisfies the premium use-rights requirement.
claims.quote: While Power Apps Premium, Power Apps per app plans, and the Power Apps per app pay-as-you-go meter that give premium Power Apps usage rights satisfy the requirement generally, use rights differ by license and by the context the app runs in.

claims.where: Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: An environment's privacy setting can override individual error-reporting preferences for the entire organization.
claims.quote: As an administrator, you can override their preferences and set error reporting preferences for the entire organization. You can prevent users from making changes in how errors are reported and change the default behavior for error reporting.

claims.where: Governance controls: related Privacy tab control
claims.claim: The privacy control path is Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Privacy + Security > Privacy preferences > Default action to take when an error occurs.
claims.quote: In the command bar, select Settings. Expand Product, and then select Privacy + Security. Under Privacy preferences, select a Default action to take when an error occurs.

claims.where: Governance controls: related Privacy tab control
claims.claim: Updating privacy and security settings requires the System Administrator security role or equivalent permissions.
claims.quote: Make sure you have the System Administrator security role or equivalent permissions to update the settings.
